attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing estimate is a cutoff-uniform signed bound on Lambda_-(sigma,ell) and on Tail_{sigma,ell}(z), including corner/cusp path-ordering terms, in the actual Yang-Mills measure.
steps: Expand each reflected Wilson hairpin as a heat-kernel plaquette-sheet exponential and keep the fourth flux order contributing to the post-H,K polarization R.
Subtract the two-pair Wick contractions; their contribution is a positive Gram form and cannot be the endpoint falsifier.
Use the null-channel incidence identity to cancel the straight-segment C_A f f commutator contact, leaving only endpoint and corner boxes plus a tail.
Localize the remaining support with a partition of unity around each boundary endpoint v and parallel transport all flux insertions to v before taking the singlet color projection.
The normalized fundamental trace gives the color prefactor (g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2, while all geometry is carried by endpoint incidence tensors J_v(z).
Taking the negative spectral part of the finite endpoint cumulant matrix gives the lower bound by Lambda_-(sigma,ell) I_partial(z).
The connected four-flux cumulant has no Gaussian term after Wick subtraction, so its first UV contribution is controlled by C_A g_R^2(ell^{-1}) times an endpoint vertex kernel.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The reduction is valid finite-dimensional spectral algebra, but it does not yet compute the endpoint eigenvalue or prove that the perturbative OPE bound dominates nonperturbatively for the required endpoint scale.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Post-H,K endpoint kappa_4 spectral bound for reflected Wilson hairpins

assumptions: Heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulation is used, with a << sigma << ell smaller than the separation between distinct nonincident endpoint boxes.
Flux insertions are parallel transported to the endpoint before color contraction, so the endpoint cumulant is gauge invariant after singlet projection.
Wick-square contractions have been separated as a positive Gram contribution and do not enter the negative endpoint spectrum.
The straight-segment nonabelian f f contact cancels in the null incidence channel already isolated for the first hairpin block.
Endpoint tails outside the boxes satisfy a uniform cluster/OPE remainder bound Tail_{sigma,ell}(z).
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated SU(N) Yang-Mills Wilson hairpin block with lattice cutoff a, smearing scale sigma, endpoint boxes Box_v(ell), and locked fundamental trace normalization.
target object: the signed endpoint contribution to the corrected second-order Schur-Feshbach null-channel form after the H,K Wilson collar data are known.

controlled interface: replace symbolic R_ij by the singlet-projected connected four-flux cumulant localized in endpoint boxes, with explicit color factor (g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and geometric incidence tensors J_v.
same-theory condition: the endpoint-box limit uses the same Wilson-loop renormalization, the same gauge-invariant test algebra, and no added boundary counterterm at the reflection plane.

equations.label: endpoint connected four-flux cumulant
equations.valid_when: Valid when the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator parallel-transports all flux insertions to the endpoint before color-singlet projection.

equations.label: endpoint R decomposition
equations.valid_when: Applies after diagonal normalization, Wick-square Gram removal, and straight f f incidence cancellation have been performed.

equations.label: negative-spectrum endpoint bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when Lambda_- is the largest negative eigenvalue magnitude of every endpoint cumulant matrix in the regulated boxes.

equations.label: ultraviolet endpoint OPE size test
equations.valid_when: Valid in the ultraviolet endpoint-box regime where the connected four-flux OPE is asymptotically free and no new cusp counterterm is introduced.

equations.label: promotion inequality
equations.valid_when: Requires the same-theory boundary OPE and the previously computed positive Gaussian margin for this finite hairpin block.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A measured or proved endpoint eigenvector aligned with J_v(z) that violates the promotion inequality is a valid same-theory falsifier for the finite Wilson block.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is contribution-making move (3): it converts the post-H,K R/kappa_4 endpoint term into a signed spectral estimate with named regulator, cumulant, cancellations, color factor, and promotion inequality.
candidate_lemmas.statement: In the first three-hairpin Wilson block, after H,K and the corrected Schur-Feshbach form are fixed, the remaining dangerous R contribution is a finite endpoint-box spectral problem: the null-channel endpoint term is bounded below by the negative spectrum of the singlet connected four-flux cumulant times an explicit endpoint incidence norm, plus a tail.

assumptions: Endpoint boxes are small enough for the renormalized local OPE to be used.
Standard Wilson cusp and perimeter factors are fixed before forming the OS quotient matrix.
The path-ordering commutator contact on straight segments has the null-incidence cancellation already checked.
definitions: C^{(4),sigma}_conn denotes the four-flux cumulant after subtracting all two-flux Wick contractions.
V^{(4),sigma}_v denotes the regulated one-interaction endpoint kernel from cubic/quartic Yang-Mills vertices and path-ordering commutators.
Lambda_- measures only the negative spectrum of the irreducible singlet endpoint matrix.

equations.label: irreducible endpoint expansion
equations.valid_when: Applies in endpoint boxes whose size is in the ultraviolet scaling window and whose Wilson renormalization is unchanged.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the regulated connected endpoint cumulant has an O(1) negative part after Wick subtraction, then either the OPE estimate fails or a boundary counterterm has entered.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This explains why the endpoint falsifier must be an irreducible nonabelian kappa_4 effect, not a hidden Gaussian Wick-square artifact.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the endpoint-box cumulant, the Gaussian order contributes only Wick pairings already accounted for by the positive Gram term; the irreducible connected endpoint spectrum starts at the nonabelian interaction order governed by C_A and the running coupling at scale ell^{-1}.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if the endpoint cumulant is regulator dependent, needs a boundary counterterm, or violates the promotion inequality by a stable negative eigenvalue.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if Lambda_-(sigma,ell) obeys the C_A g_R^2 endpoint OPE bound and the color-incidence weighted negative part plus tails is below M_G uniformly in the cutoff.
control_decision.reason: The branch is contribution-making: it has reduced the post-H,K R term to a concrete regulated spectral computation and a first UV size test.

dependency_updates.description: R is now represented as a singlet connected four-flux endpoint spectral problem with prefactor (g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and incidence norm I_partial(z).
The regulator is needed to define flux insertions, endpoint boxes, Wick-square subtraction, and the same endpoint cumulant on both sides of reflection.
The cancellation removes bulk straight-segment commutator contacts; it must still be checked with exact path ordering at endpoint cutoffs.
Need a cutoff-uniform signed estimate for Lambda_-(sigma,ell) and corner tails, not only a formal cumulant definition.

falsifiers: A lattice heat-kernel endpoint measurement finds Lambda_- I_partial large enough that the endpoint term exceeds the positive Gaussian margin; this is the direct finite-block falsifier.
A residual straight-segment f f contact survives after exact path ordering, invalidating the cancellation used before endpoint localization.
The endpoint tail is not local because a boundary mode produces power leakage between distinct endpoint boxes.
Wilson cusp renormalization at the reflection plane requires a new boundary counterterm, so the same-theory condition is false even if positivity is restored.
The irreducible four-flux cumulant contains an O(1) negative contact after Wick subtraction, contradicting the UV endpoint OPE size test.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: The branch did not restate the threshold. It identified the actual Yang-Mills object that remains: the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet singlet connected four-flux endpoint cumulant. Wick-square terms are safe positive Gram terms, and straight f f contacts cancel in the null incidence channel. The remaining valid promotion or falsifier is a finite endpoint negative-spectrum inequality with explicit color factor, incidence norm, and tail.
